claim.pdf_says: UNLOCK file-name-1 [ RECORD / RECORDS ]  (one line: UNLOCK, then file-name-1, then a bracket stacking RECORD over RECORDS)
claim.why_it_matters: The 14.9.43.1 general format puts file-name-1 on a separate row beneath UNLOCK, so the drawing reads as UNLOCK followed by the RECORD/RECORDS bracket with file-name-1 dangling or stacked under UNLOCK; the operand order UNLOCK file-name-1 [RECORD|RECORDS] is not shown on one line as the standard prints it.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (PDF p629, printed 605) shows 'UNLOCK file-name-1' with UNLOCK underlined, followed by a square bracket that stacks RECORD over RECORDS, with no choice-indicator bars. The markdown keeps every element: UNLOCK is underlined, file-name-1 is a mandatory operand outside the bracket, and the bracket (drawn with box corners) stacks RECORD over RECORDS with no bars, so it is still the optional at-most-one choice of §2014:5.2.5.1. The only difference is where file-name-1 sits in the ASCII drawing: on the bracket's last row at column 0, not on the UNLOCK row. It is not enclosed in any brace or bracket, nothing stacks it as an alternative to UNLOCK, and reading left to right it still comes before the bracket. This is a layout and alignment artifact that does not change the syntax, so it does not count as a content discrepancy.
